whatItIs.text: A tender leafy green of the amaranth family, eaten raw or cooked; its flavour changes completely between the two, and blanching tames its oxalates.

historyNote.text: Spinach probably arose about 2,000 years ago around Iran and reached China via Nepal; Arabs brought it to Sicily in 827 CE, a 12th-century Iberian writer called it 'the chieftain of leafy greens', and it appears in England's first cookbook, the Forme of Cury (1390), as 'spynoches'.

howToChoose.text: Choose crisp, deep-green leaves with firm stems and no sliminess; baby spinach needs no stemming, mature bunches taste better and cost less.

storage.text: Refrigerate dry and loosely bagged, unwashed until use.

useItUp.text: Wilted spinach vanishes into dals, lasagnas, and smoothies; sauté with garlic and lemon, and squeeze the water out for anything baked.

substitutions.note: use in cooked dishes; squeeze dry
